# Test fixtures

Binary matrices in the container format `BinaryMatrix` reads, used by the golden tests in
`MelSpectrogramTests.cpp` and `ZeroPhaseFilterTests.cpp`.

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `test_signal.bin` | 2 s of deterministic test audio at 16 kHz: noise, a 220 Hz and a 1760 Hz tone, and 25 Hz rumble below the high-pass corner |
| `expected_log_mel.bin` | Its log-mel spectrogram, computed by NumPy with librosa's HTK filter bank |
| `expected_high_pass.bin` | The same signal through `scipy.signal.filtfilt` |
| `mel_filter_bank.bin` | librosa's `[128, 513]` HTK mel bank |

These are what make the C++ front end *verifiable* rather than merely plausible: they would
catch a symmetric Hann window where a periodic one belongs, power instead of magnitude, a
missing reflection, or a transposed filter bank — all of which produce a valid-looking
spectrogram of the wrong thing.

They were generated by the Python exporter that used to live in `tools/`, removed in the
commit after b6ea4bd. To regenerate or audit them, recover it:

    git checkout b6ea4bd -- tools
    cd tools && PYTHONPATH=. python -m rvcara_export.reference

Until then treat them as fixed inputs. Changing the DSP they cover means either matching
them or recovering the exporter and regenerating them deliberately.
